stages.title: Hold, Fret, and Tune
stages.description: The guitar stays still so the fretting hand can press strings, not hold the instrument up. Tune before you play, and put each finger just behind the fret.
learningObjectives: Set the guitar so the fretting hand is free
Fret with the fingertips, close to the fret
Tune before a practice session
Play a major scale with the whole-step and half-step pattern

explainBack.question: A new player leans the guitar back, presses with the side of the thumb, and starts practicing on a guitar that is out of tune. Explain how to hold and fret the instrument, why a tuner comes first, and how to find a major scale from any note.
rubric: Use a strap or a stable sitting position so the guitar does not move, and do not support the guitar with the fretting hand
Leaning the guitar back forces the wrist around the neck and adds tension
Fret with the fingertips, thumb flat behind the neck, and place the finger just behind the fret without touching it
Tune at the start of practice; a tuner is the reliable check
Each fret is a half step, and a whole step is two frets
A major scale follows whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half from any starting note

resources.title: How to Start Learning Your Guitar Scales
resources.author: Larry Baione
resources.description: Berklee's starting points for holding the guitar, fretting cleanly, and playing a major scale.
keyPoints: Use a strap so the guitar stays in the same place sitting or standing
Hold the guitar in a way that feels natural and does not strain the shoulder
Fret with the fingertips, keep the thumb flat behind the neck, and use the pad of the thumb as a fulcrum
A rest stroke lets the pick come to rest on the next string and gives more control
Tune at the start of every practice session
Each fret is a half step; a major scale is whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half

resources.title: Body Posture and Finger Placement Exercise (Guitar Lesson BC-106) Guitar for beginners
resources.description: Where to sit the guitar, and the rule for placing a finger next to the fret.
keyPoints: Rest the guitar on the leg on the same side as the strumming hand, unless you are using a classical position
Keep the guitar upright and close to the body
A strap keeps an electric guitar in place when you stand
Place the fretting finger as close to the fret as you can without touching the fret

stages.title: How Guitar Music Is Written
stages.description: Guitarists meet three kinds of writing: staff notation, tablature, and fretboard diagrams. Each one shows something the others leave out.
learningObjectives: Read a fret number on the right string in tab
Read a chord diagram, including muted strings and a barre
Explain what tab does not show
Name the strings in standard tuning

explainBack.question: A friend sends you a tab that says 3 on the A string, plus a chord diagram with an x over the low E string and a slur across several strings at the 3rd fret. Explain what each mark means, what the tab is not telling you, and how the strings are named in standard tuning.
rubric: In tab, six lines are the six strings, the top line is the high E, and a number is the fret, with 0 for an open string
A 3 on the A string is C, three half steps above A
Tab usually does not show rhythm
Standard tuning is E A D G B E, low to high
On a chord diagram, a dot is a fretted note, an open circle is an open string, and an x means mute that string
A slur across strings means one finger holds them down, which is a barre

resources.title: Guitar Notation Basics
resources.author: Jonathan Feist
resources.description: How staff notation, tablature, and chord diagrams each describe the same guitar part.
keyPoints: String 6 is the low E and string 1 is the high E; uncircled numbers are plucking fingers
Tab uses six lines, high E on top, and a number for the fret, with 0 for an open string
Each fret is a half step, so a 3 on the A string is the note C
Tab usually does not show rhythm
If the tuning is not standard EADGBE, the string notes are written at the left of the tab
A chord diagram's x means mute, an open dot means an open string, and a slur across strings is a barre

stages.title: Your First Chord
stages.description: A chord is only useful if every note rings. Learn one open chord, leave out the strings marked x, and check the notes one at a time.
learningObjectives: Finger an open D chord
Skip the strings a diagram marks with an x
Check each note before you strum
Name the fingers used to fret

explainBack.question: You are learning an open D chord and one note buzzes. Explain which strings you play, how you check the chord, and what you change before you call it ready.
rubric: The two lowest strings of an open D chord are not played
The strum starts on the fourth string
Check the chord by picking each note on its own, then fix the finger that buzzes
Fingers are numbered 1 to 4 from index to pinkie; the thumb is not numbered
A buzzing note usually means the finger is not close enough to the fret or is touching a neighbor string

resources.title: Super Easy First Guitar Lesson - Guitar Lessons For Beginners - Stage 1 - The D Chord
resources.description: How to place an open D chord and how to hear whether every note is clean.
keyPoints: An open D chord leaves out the two lowest strings, which a diagram marks with an x
Start the strum on the fourth string
Pick the notes one at a time and move the finger that makes a note buzz
Strum again only after each note rings on its own

stages.title: Time and the First Strum
stages.description: Songs are counted in beats. Most beginner guitar parts are in four, and the first job is to land a downstrum on beat 1.
learningObjectives: Explain what a beat and a measure are
Read a 4/4 time signature
Count a bar as 1, 2, 3, 4
Strum on beat 1 and keep counting through the bar

explainBack.question: A song is in 4/4 and you keep changing chords late. Explain what 4/4 means, how you count a bar, and how a first strumming pattern uses beat 1 so the chord change lands on time.
rubric: A beat is a pulse that keeps coming back; a measure is one group of those beats
In a simple meter the beat divides in two
In 4/4 the top number means four beats in a measure and the bottom number means a quarter note is the beat
Count the bar 1, 2, 3, 4, and count the division of a beat as and
The first strum is a downstrum on beat 1, while the hand keeps the count going
Change chords so the next downstrum still lands on 1

resources.title: Simple Meter and Time Signatures
resources.description: A free textbook chapter on beats, measures, and how to read a simple time signature.
keyPoints: A beat is a regularly recurring pulse
In a simple meter the beat divides into two, then into four
Duple, triple, and quadruple meters group beats in twos, threes, and fours
A measure is one group of beats, separated from the next by a bar line
In a simple time signature the top number is how many beats are in the measure and the bottom number is the note that gets the beat
In 4/4, count quarter notes as 1, 2, 3, 4, and count the second eighth note of a beat as and

resources.title: Your FIRST Strumming Pattern EVER! | Guitar for Beginners
resources.description: Why the first strumming pattern is a single downstrum on beat 1.
keyPoints: Early beginner songs in this course are in 4/4
Count 1, 2, 3, 4 and strum down only on 1
Keep the count going on the beats you do not strum
The goal is to land that downstrum on beat 1 when the chord changes

stages.title: Fingerstyle and Tone
stages.description: Fingerstyle plays a chord one note at a time. Where the hand sits between the fingerboard and the bridge changes the tone.
learningObjectives: Separate an arpeggio from a strum
Alternate the picking fingers
Use a metronome slowly enough to stay relaxed
Change tone by moving the hand toward the fingerboard or the bridge

explainBack.question: You want a song to sound like the notes of a chord played one by one, and a friend says to play it faster until it sounds smooth. Explain how to practice an arpeggio, which fingers do the work, and how to make the same strum sweeter or brighter.
rubric: An arpeggio plays the notes of a chord one after another instead of together
The fretting hand can hold one shape while the picking hand moves, and the same picking finger does not play twice in a row
Practice with a metronome at a tempo where the hand stays relaxed; speed comes after that
Stop if the hand gets tired
Playing nearer the fingerboard (sul tasto) is rounder; playing nearer the bridge (ponticello) is brighter
The usual spot is between those two, near the bridge side of the soundhole

resources.title: Acoustic Guitar Techniques to Move Past Beginner Level
resources.author: Abigail Aronson Zocher
resources.description: Fingerstyle, practice with a metronome, and how the picking hand's position changes the sound.
keyPoints: Standard tuning is EADGBE; anything else is an alternate tuning
An arpeggio plays chord notes one after another, usually without repeating the same picking finger twice in a row
Set the metronome where the picking hand stays relaxed, and put the thumb note in the middle of the click
Relaxation comes before speed, and you stop when the hand is tired
Classical names for the picking fingers are p, i, m, and a: thumb, index, middle, and ring
Sul tasto, over the fingerboard, is rounder; ponticello, near the bridge, is brighter

stages.title: Chord Symbols
stages.description: A chord symbol names the notes without naming a key. A letter alone is a major triad, and extra marks change the quality or add notes.
learningObjectives: Read a bare letter as a major triad
Tell a chord symbol from a Roman numeral
Explain the default seventh, ninth, and eleventh
Assume root position unless a bass note is written

explainBack.question: A chart shows C, then C7, then C13, and a friend treats C7 as C with a major seventh. Explain what each symbol asks for, and how that differs from a Roman numeral in a key.
rubric: A letter with nothing after it is a major triad
Chord symbols name exact notes and do not depend on a key; Roman numerals show a chord's place in a key
Symbols assume the bass is the root unless another bass note is written
The default seventh is minor, so C7 contains B-flat, not B
Ninths and thirteenths are major, and elevenths are perfect, unless the symbol says otherwise

resources.title: Chord Symbols
resources.description: How pop and jazz chord symbols name a root, a quality, and any added notes.
keyPoints: A chord symbol gives the root, the triad quality, any extensions, and a non-root bass note if there is one
A note name alone means a major triad
Chord symbols are absolute; Roman numerals are relative to a key
The symbol assumes the chord is in root position unless a different bass note is shown
The default seventh is minor; ninths and thirteenths default to major, and elevenths to perfect

stages.title: Triads in a Key
stages.description: In a major key, the chord on each scale degree has a fixed quality. That pattern is what makes G, C, and D major in the key of G, and E minor, A minor, and B minor beside them.
learningObjectives: Build a triad on each degree of a major scale
Name which degrees are major, minor, and diminished
Move that pattern to another major key
Explain why the pattern does not change when the key does

explainBack.question: You are in G major and the song uses chords on G, A, B, C, D, E, and F-sharp. Explain which of those triads are major, which are minor, which is diminished, and why the same pattern appears in every major key.
rubric: A triad stacks two thirds on a root
In a major key, triads on degrees 1, 4, and 5 are major
Triads on degrees 2, 3, and 6 are minor
The triad on degree 7 is diminished
In G major that means G, C, and D are major, A, B, and E are minor, and F-sharp is diminished
The qualities stay the same in every major key because they come from the scale degrees, not from one key's letter names

resources.title: Triads
resources.description: Which triad quality sits on each degree of a major scale.
keyPoints: A chord symbol starts with the root, then marks the triad's quality
In a major key, triads on do, fa, and sol are major
Triads on re, mi, and la are minor
The triad on ti is diminished
Those qualities do not change from key to key: the triad on degree 1 of any major key is major

stages.title: Pentatonic Shapes
stages.description: The pentatonic scale has five notes and no half steps. Rock guitar often puts a major chord, or a barre shape, on each of those notes.
learningObjectives: Describe the major and minor pentatonic scales
Explain why a pentatonic collection has no half steps
Use pentatonic notes as chord roots
Explain why parallel barre chords fit the guitar

explainBack.question: A riff uses five notes and never a fret right next to the last one, and the chords are the same major shape moved up the neck. Explain what scale that describes, and why that chord habit fits the guitar.
rubric: A pentatonic scale has five pitches
The common pentatonic collections have no half steps
Major pentatonic and minor pentatonic are two rotations of that five-note collection
In rock, those scale notes are often used as chord roots
The chords on those roots may be major, minor, or power chords, so the full sound is not always pentatonic
The same major shape slid up the neck is a barre chord, which is why this pattern fits guitar

resources.title: Pentatonic Harmony
resources.description: How five-note scales become chord roots, including the parallel barre chords common on guitar.
keyPoints: The pentatonic collection has five pitches and no half steps
In popular music the two common rotations are major pentatonic and minor pentatonic
A pentatonic chord system often uses those scale notes as chord roots
The chords can be major, minor, power chords, or chords with added notes
Because the chord quality can vary, the notes actually sounding are often not only the pentatonic scale
Parallel major barre chords on pentatonic roots sit naturally on the guitar

name: Guitar
description: Hold the guitar without strain, read a chord diagram, fret an open chord in time, and use scales, fingerstyle, and chord symbols to move past the first songs.
